newsitem.title: USA: FORMER OCTEL INSIDER FINED FOR TRADES -SEC.
newsitem.headline: FORMER OCTEL INSIDER FINED FOR TRADES -SEC.

text.p: A former Octel Communications Corp official was ordered by a federal judge to pay $505,819 plus interest to settle charges of insider trading, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on Wednesday said.

The court found that Shahryar Soroosh of Sacramento, California, the company's former senior software engineer, "amassed a substantial short position in the stock and options of Octel," knowing before any announcement that Octel planned to delay the release of computer software it was developing, the SEC said.

"His trading activity and the circumstances surrounding it were consistent with the possession of insider knowledge, and he has offered no plausible explanation otherwise," the judge wrote in his August 5 opinion, which follows a four-day bench trial held earlier this year.
According to the SEC, shares of the company, which produces voice-processing systems, dropped by more than 35 percent after its public announcement of the software delay.

"As a result, Soroosh realized profits of over $500,000, based on his 35,000-share short position and his 80 put contracts, all of which he had accumulated in the weeks before the announcement," the SEC said.
The SEC said the court had rejected Soroosh's defense that his trading was part of a pattern, finding that the activity in question was out of the ordinary.
Soroosh could not be immediately reached for comment.
